Kazi HR Policy Document

1. Leave Policy
Employees are entitled to 20 days of paid leave per year. 
Sick leave requires a medical certificate if longer than 2 days.
Maternity leave is 3 months fully paid.

Salaries are paid on the 25th of every month.
Performance bonuses are reviewed annually in December.

3. Code of Conduct
Employees must maintain a professional demeanor at all times.
Remote work is allowed up to 3 days a week with manager approval.

EMPLOYMENT POLICY 
Kazi Technologies Ltd – Uganda 
 
1.1 Employment Types 
Kazi Technologies Ltd recognizes multiple forms of employment to support operational 
flexibility while ensuring fairness and compliance with Ugandan labor standards. 
1.1.1 Full-Time Employees 
Full-time employees are engaged on a permanent basis and are expected to work standard 
company hours. 
Terms: 
• Work 40–45 hours per week  
• Eligible for full company benefits (leave, NSSF , bonuses)

• Entitled to paid leave and statutory protections  
• Must adhere to all company policies and performance standards  
 
1.1.2 Part-Time Employees 
Part-time employees work fewer hours than full-time employees. 
Terms: 
• Work less than 40 hours per week  
• Compensation is prorated based on hours worked  
• May receive limited benefits depending on contract terms  
• Leave entitlements are calculated proportionally  
 
1.1.3 Contract Employees

1.1.3 Contract Employees 
Contract employees are hired for a fixed duration or specific project. 
Terms: • Governed by a signed contract agreement  
• Not entitled to full employee benefits unless specified  
• Payment structure defined in contract (monthly, milestone-based, etc.)  
• Contract automatically ends upon completion or expiry unless renewed  
 
1.1.4 Interns 
Interns are engaged for training and development purposes. 
Terms: 
• Duration typically 3–6 months

Terms: 
• Duration typically 3–6 months  
• May receive stipend or allowance  
• Not classified as permanent employees  
• Expected to follow company rules and confidentiality standards  
 
1.2 Probation Period 
All new employees undergo a probationary period to assess suitability for the role. 
1.2.1 Duration 
• Standard probation period: 6 months  
 
1.2.2 Evaluation During Probation 
Employees will be evaluated based on: 
• Job performance  
• Attendance and punctuality

• Attendance and punctuality  
• Behavioral alignment with company values  
• Ability to meet KPIs  
 
1.2.3 Extension of Probation • Probation may be extended by up to 3 months  
• Extension is applied when:  
o Performance is borderline  
o More time is needed for evaluation  
 
1.2.4 Confirmation of Employment 
• Upon successful completion, employee receives written confirmation  
• Gains full employment status and benefits  
 
1.2.5 Termination During Probation

1.2.5 Termination During Probation 
• Either party may terminate employment with shorter notice (e.g., 1 week)  
• No obligation for full notice period during probation  
 
1.3 Working Hours 
Kazi Technologies Ltd maintains structured working hours to ensure productivity and work-
life balance. 
 
1.3.1 Standard Working Schedule 
• Monday to Friday  
• 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM  
• Includes a 1-hour lunch break  
 
1.3.2 Flexibility 
• Flexible start/end times may be approved by management

• Employees must still complete required daily hours  
 1.3.3 Overtime 
• Overtime must be pre-approved  
• Compensated according to payroll policy  
• Not guaranteed and subject to operational need  
 
1.3.4 Attendance Requirements 
Employees must: 
• Report to work on time  
• Notify supervisors in case of lateness or absence  
• Record attendance where required  
 
1.3.5 Public Holidays 
• Employees are entitled to Ugandan public holidays

• Work on public holidays must be approved and compensated  
 
1.4 Remote Work Policy 
Kazi Technologies Ltd supports flexible working arrangements where appropriate. 
 
1.4.1 Eligibility 
Remote work is: 
• Not automatic  
• Granted based on:  
o Role suitability  
o Performance history  
o Manager approval  
 1.4.2 Approval Process 
• Employee submits request to supervisor  
• Supervisor evaluates:  
o Productivity impact  
o Team collaboration needs  
• Final approval documented

• Final approval documented  
 
1.4.3 Expectations While Working Remotely 
Employees must: 
• Be available during working hours  
• Respond to communication promptly (email, Slack, etc.)  
• Attend virtual meetings  
• Deliver assigned tasks on time  
 
1.4.4 Equipment and Connectivity 
• Employees are responsible for:  
o Reliable internet connection  
o Safe working environment  
• Company may provide equipment where necessary  
 
1.4.5 Performance Monitoring

1.4.5 Performance Monitoring 
• Output-based evaluation (not just hours)

o Performance drops  
o Communication is poor  
 1.4.6 Data Security 
While working remotely:

5.1 Purpose of the Disciplinary Policy 
Kazi Technologies Ltd is committed to maintaining a professional, productive, and 
respectful work environment. The disciplinary policy provides a fair and consistent 
framework for addressing employee misconduct, performance concerns, and violations of 
company policies. 
The purpose of disciplinary action is to: 
• Correct inappropriate behavior

• Promote accountability 
• Maintain workplace standards

5.2 Grounds for Disciplinary Action 
Employees may be subject to disciplinary action for conduct or behavior that negatively 
affects: 
• Workplace operations 
• Company reputation 
• Employee safety 
• Compliance with company policies 
 
5.2.1 Misconduct

5.2.1 Misconduct 
Misconduct refers to inappropriate or unacceptable behavior in the workplace. 
Examples include: 
• Insubordination 
• Disrespectful behavior • Use of offensive language 
• Failure to follow lawful instructions 
• Unprofessional conduct 
• Misuse of company resources 
 
5.2.2 Poor Performance 
Employees are expected to perform duties competently and meet agreed performance 
standards. 
Performance-related disciplinary action may arise from: 
• Failure to meet KPIs

• Failure to meet KPIs 
• Repeated mistakes 
• Negligence 
• Low productivity 
• Failure to improve after coaching or feedback 
The company will generally provide reasonable support and performance improvement 
opportunities before escalating disciplinary action. 
 
5.2.3 Absenteeism and Lateness 
Employees are required to maintain acceptable attendance and punctuality. 
Disciplinary action may result from: 
• Repeated unexplained absences 
• Chronic lateness

• Chronic lateness 
• Failure to notify supervisors of absence 
• Leaving work without authorization 
 
5.2.4 Violation of Company Policies 
Employees must comply with all organizational policies and procedures. Examples of policy violations include: 
• Breach of IT policy 
• Confidentiality violations 
• Unauthorized disclosure of information 
• Failure to comply with safety procedures 
• Conflict of interest violations 
 
5.3 Disciplinary Process

5.3 Disciplinary Process 
Kazi Technologies Ltd follows a progressive disciplinary process aimed at correcting 
behavior where possible. 
The severity of disciplinary action depends on: 
• Nature of misconduct 
• Frequency of incidents 
• Employee disciplinary history 
• Impact on the organization 
 
Step 1: Verbal Warning 
A verbal warning may be issued for minor first-time offenses. 
The supervisor or manager will: 
• Discuss the issue with the employee 
• Explain expected improvements

• Explain expected improvements 
• Document the discussion internally where appropriate 
 
Step 2: Written Warning 
If misconduct continues or the issue is more serious, a written warning may be issued. 
The written warning will include: • Details of the misconduct or issue 
• Previous corrective actions taken 
• Required improvements 
• Timeline for improvement 
• Consequences of further violations 
Employees may be required to acknowledge receipt of the warning.

Step 3: Final Written Warning 
A final written warning may be issued where: 
• Previous warnings failed to resolve the issue 
• The misconduct is serious but does not warrant immediate termination 
The final warning will clearly state that further violations may result in termination of 
employment. 
 
Step 4: Termination of Employment 
Employment may be terminated where: 
• Misconduct persists despite warnings 
• Serious violations occur

• Serious violations occur 
• Trust and working relationships are irreparably damaged 
Termination will be handled in accordance with employment contracts and Ugandan labor 
laws. 
 
5.4 Investigation Procedures 
Before major disciplinary action is taken, the company may conduct an investigation. 
Investigations may include: 
• Interviews 
• Review of evidence • Examination of records or systems 
• Witness statements

• Witness statements 
Employees may be asked to provide explanations or participate in disciplinary meetings. 
 
5.5 Employee Right to Respond 
Employees have the right to: 
• Be informed of allegations against them 
• Respond to accusations 
• Present supporting evidence 
• Request clarification during disciplinary proceedings 
The company will consider all relevant information before making disciplinary decisions. 
 
5.6 Suspension Pending Investigation

5.6 Suspension Pending Investigation 
In serious cases, employees may be suspended while investigations are conducted. 
Suspension: 
• May be with pay 
• Is not considered disciplinary action by itself 
• Is intended to protect workplace integrity and investigations 
 
5.7 Gross Misconduct 
Gross misconduct refers to extremely serious behavior that fundamentally breaches trust 
and company standards. 
Gross misconduct may result in immediate termination without prior warnings.

Examples of Gross Misconduct 
Theft • Stealing company, client, or employee property 
• Unauthorized possession of company assets 
 
Fraud 
• Falsifying records 
• Payroll fraud 
• Financial dishonesty 
• Misrepresentation for personal gain 
 
Violence and Threats 
• Physical assault 
• Threatening behavior 
• Workplace intimidation 
• Possession of dangerous weapons on company premises 
 
Serious Breach of Confidentiality 
• Unauthorized disclosure of sensitive company or client information

• Sharing payroll or employee data without authorization 
• Leaking proprietary or confidential documents 
 
Additional Examples of Gross Misconduct 
Other serious offenses may include: 
• Deliberate damage to company property 
• Serious harassment or discrimination 
• Accessing systems without authorization 
• Serious violation of IT security policies • Reporting to work under the influence of illegal substances 
 
5.8 Appeals Process

5.8 Appeals Process 
Employees may appeal disciplinary decisions if they believe: 
• Procedures were unfair 
• Evidence was inaccurate 
• The disciplinary outcome was unreasonable 
Appeals must: 
• Be submitted in writing 
• Clearly state reasons for appeal 
• Be filed within the timeframe specified by HR 
The company will review appeals fairly and communicate the final decision formally. 
 
5.9 Record Keeping 
The company maintains disciplinary records for administrative and legal purposes.

Records may include: 
• Warnings issued 
• Investigation findings 
• Employee responses 
• Final outcomes 
Disciplinary records are treated as confidential and accessed only by authorized 
personnel. 
 
5.10 Policy Compliance 
All employees are expected to: 
• Understand this disciplinary policy • Cooperate with investigations 
• Maintain professional conduct at all times 
Failure to comply with disciplinary procedures may itself result in further disciplinary 
action.
